title: [Compound Danshen Cataplasm promoting acclimatization to high-altitude environments].
authors: Chen, Yu-Ting; Niu, Hong; Wang, Jing-Zhe; Li, Meng-Zhen; Guo, Jin; Jin, Yi-Guang; DU, Li-Na
journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
one_liner_zh: 该文研究复方丹参贴膏抗高原缺氧作用，虽含分子对接但对象为药物-蛋白靶点，非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: To address acute mountain sickness(AMS) easily induced by low pressure, hypoxia, and intense ultraviolet radiation in high-altitude environments, a novel Compound Danshen Cataplasm(CDC) was developed, and its adhesive properties were evaluated. The hippocampal neuron(HT22) hypoxia model and small-animal hypoxia model were established. The anti-hypoxia and anti-AMS efficacy of CDC was assessed by an open field test, novel object recognition test, routine blood examination, sleep duration measurement, determination of brain and lung wet-to-dry ratios, detection of inflammatory and oxidative stress factors, and pathological section observation. In addition, network pharmacology and molecular docking simulations were employed to explore the underlying mechanism of action. The results show that CDC can significantly increase the survival rate of HT22 cells under hypoxia, reduce cell apoptosis, improve spontaneous exploration ability and cognitive function of hypoxic model mice, prolong sleep duration under hypoxic conditions, promote blood cell recovery, alleviate brain and lung edema, significantly reduce the levels of TNF-alpha, i NOS, IL-6, and MDA in blood, brain tissue, and lung tissue of mice, increase SOD activity(P<0. 01), and markedly alleviate hypoxia-induced brain and lung edema as well as inflammatory cell infiltration. Network pharmacology results reveal that the binding energies between key active components of CDC and core disease targets are all less than-5 k J.mol~(-1), and that CDC can downregulate the protein expression levels of relevant genes STAT3, JAK1, JAK2, and their phosphorylated forms in the brain tissue of mice. In conclusion, CDC can meet the need for prolonged efficacy under urgent and special conditions, demonstrating significant potential application value.
abstract_zh: 为解决高海拔环境中低压、缺氧及强紫外线辐射易诱发急性高山病（acute mountain sickness, AMS）的问题，研制了一种新型复方丹参贴膏（Compound Danshen Cataplasm, CDC），并对其黏附性能进行了评价。建立了海马神经元（HT22）缺氧模型和小动物缺氧模型。通过旷场实验、新物体识别实验、血常规检查、睡眠时间测定、脑肺湿干比测定、炎症及氧化应激因子检测以及病理切片观察，评估了CDC的抗缺氧和抗AMS疗效。此外，采用网络药理学和分子对接模拟探讨了其潜在作用机制。结果表明，CDC能显著提高HT22细胞在缺氧条件下的存活率，减少细胞凋亡，改善缺氧模型小鼠的自发探索能力和认知功能，延长缺氧条件下的睡眠时间，促进血细胞恢复，减轻脑肺水肿，显著降低小鼠血液、脑组织和肺组织中TNF-α、iNOS、IL-6和MDA的水平，增加SOD活性（P<0.01），并明显缓解缺氧诱导的脑肺水肿及炎症细胞浸润。网络药理学结果显示，CDC关键活性成分与核心疾病靶点之间的结合能均小于-5 kJ·mol⁻¹，且CDC能下调小鼠脑组织中相关基因STAT3、JAK1、JAK2及其磷酸化形式的蛋白表达水平。总之，CDC能满足紧急和特殊条件下长效作用的需求，显示出显著的应用潜力。
